artifact: DataVine worker-enforced cache capacity and recovery checkpoint

build.command: cd /users/jzhou24/cctools_repo/datavine/taskvine/src && make clean && make -j8 && make install

rejected_results: A build whose install submake printed Text file busy while orphan local workers held the installed executable was rejected and repeated after killing the exact orphan PIDs.
A sequential factory run that reused one catalog project name across managers was rejected because stale catalog records contaminated worker assignment.

Evicting future-used volatile IData merely because another Controller source existed was rejected because TaskVine submitted special legacy recovery tasks and a stale prune acknowledgement could target a newer realization.
proved: A cooperating Manager and worker independently enforce configured cache item and byte capacities.
Normal task output slots are reserved before execution and unpublished outputs cannot satisfy input admission.
Dispatch waits for targeted cache unlink acknowledgement before consuming the released capacity.
An oversized task output fails explicitly instead of being published outside the byte bound.
Prefetch, demand execution, eviction, worker disconnection, and one ordinary-task recovery replay coexist without exceeding the configured physical cache bounds.
The rebuilt package reproduces the recovery case on two remote factory workers.
not_proved: real worker process loss rather than Manager-triggered worker release
loss during an active byte transfer
future-used volatile IData eviction without TaskVine legacy recovery tasks
repeated recovery bounded by a durability frontier
bounded hot-path cost at Grand Challenge scale
Grand Challenge scale, mandatory failure schedule, or Legacy comparison
